newsitem.title: UK: UK OPRAF mulls 1 mln stg fine for Stagecoach.
newsitem.headline: UK OPRAF mulls 1 mln stg fine for Stagecoach.

text.p: U.K. rail watchdog Opraf said on Friday it was mulling a one million pound fine against transport group Stagecoach if it fails to run at least 98.5 percent of services scheduled for its South West Trains unit for April and May.
It said that if the fine was imposed, SWT would then face losing its franchise if it failed to run at least 97.5 percent of its services.
Stagecoach has been the focus of criticism by politicians and passengers in recent weeks after cancelling dozens of trains in recent weeks.
SWT admits that it has cancelled an average of 39 train services a day since February 1997.
Cox is due to make an appearance before the UK parliament's transport select committee next week to discuss its performance since assuming the franchise in February 1996.
In a statement after the OPRAF announcement, Stagecoach said it was confident SWT would meet the regulator's requirements.
